# FINDINGS: plugin-hive native pause/resume & runner-agnostic capabilities vs. Minerva

## FILES_EXAMINED

**Canonical repo checkout** (`/Users/mdostal/Code/plugin-hive`, remotes: `origin`=firefly-events/plugin-hive, `fork`=mdostal/plugin-hive → redirects to `mdostal/plugin-hive-fork`, a fork of firefly-events/plugin-hive):

- `hive/lib/dag_executor/executor/handlers/pause.py`
- `hive/lib/dag_executor/executor/dispatcher.py`
- `hive/lib/dag_executor/run_state/resume.py`

**Minerva repo** (`/Users/mdostal/Documents/work/pantheon/minerva`):

**GitHub (`gh` CLI)**: PR #341 firefly-events/plugin-hive (full body, files, comments, review state); `gh pr list` across firefly-events/plugin-hive (--state all --limit 60, plus keyword searches for headless/agnostic/resume/harness/opencode/plan-agnostic); `gh pr list --repo mdostal/plugin-hive-fork` (full list, 12 PRs); PR #12 and PR #10 on mdostal/plugin-hive-fork; `gh api .../contents/hive/agnostic` on both repos.

## PATTERNS_OBSERVED

**1. PR #341 "Headless question protocol + bounded Stop hook"** (firefly-events/plugin-hive#341, opened 2026-07-26, still **OPEN**, `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`, `mergeable: MERGEABLE`, `reviewDecision: ""` empty — no human approval recorded):
- Mechanism: `hive/lib/runtime_mode.{py,js}` detects headless via explicit env signals only (`HIVE_HEADLESS=1/0` wins, else `CI=true` → headless, else interactive-by-default; explicitly no TTY-probe fallback). `hive/lib/question_gateway.{py,js}` batches all questions at a phase boundary into `.pHive/questions/<skill>-<invocation-id>.yaml`, prints `AWAITING_ANSWERS`, and **exits the process**. An external orchestrator writes `answer:` + `status: answered` onto the same file; author's PR text states this "mirrors Minerva's own `submitAnswers` shape." Envelopes are **deleted on consume** (fixed in review round 3 — reuse of phase ids like `1a` across separate invocations would otherwise match stale answered envelopes forever).
- Scope: wired into 3 skills only — `kickoff` (7 phase points), `design` (2 touchpoints, loop-aware), `plan` (2 points: branch-switch-confirm, version_bump). Explicitly NOT covering `execute`, `test`, `review`, `ship`, etc. Author-noted gap: plan's newer "sidecar-retention" question (step 14c) isn't wired since it didn't exist in this repo's `develop` at PR time.
- Review state: 4 rounds of CodeRabbit automated review (no human reviewer comments/approvals present in the 19 PR comments — all are the author mdostal posting fix summaries or `@coderabbitai review` triggers). 63/63 tests passing per author's last update. One live end-to-end smoke test reported by author (`claude -p --plugin-dir`, headless kickoff round-trip through one phase) — not a full-coverage manual QA pass.
- Bounded Stop hook (`hooks/metrics-stop-dispatch.sh`) is a separate, unrelated fix in the same PR: replaces unbounded `jq -c -s` transcript slurp (benchmarked 13.57s/~7.5GB RSS on an 884MB synthetic transcript) with a streaming pass + size guard.

**2. DAG executor's native `node_type: pause`** (documented `hive/references/workflow-schema.md` lines 207-254, implemented in the 2.15.0 plugin cache):
- Mechanism is a **synchronous blocking poll loop inside a single process invocation**, not a stateless resumable ABI. `Dispatcher.dispatch()` → `PauseHandler.handle()` → `wait_for_signal()` (`pause/signal.py`) runs `while True: check sentinel files; sleep(poll_interval=5.0s)` until an `.approve`/`.reject` sentinel appears at `<runs_root>/<run_id>/pause/<node_id>.{approve,reject}` or timeout elapses. Default timeout = no user cap but a hard security ceiling of 30 days (`DEFAULT_HARD_CEILING_SECONDS`).
- Security: HMAC-SHA256 resume tokens (`pause/token.py`), bound to `(run_id, node_id)`, signing key persisted per-run at `<runs_root>/<run_id>/.signing_key` (mode 0600). Sentinel filename alone never honors the pause — sentinel body must carry the verified token (defeats forgery/replay, per "security:plan-audit" findings #1-#4, #10 referenced in code comments).
- **Cold-start / resume-from-fresh-process is explicitly NOT the model**: `run_state/resume.py`'s generic `--resume <run-id>` CLI entry point (used for replaying FAILED/interrupted runs) explicitly raises `ResumeFromInvalidStateError` if it encounters a `SUSPENDED` run — comment states `"SUSPENDED → delegated to hde-8 pause-resume path; this story raises ResumeFromInvalidStateError if encountered (hde-8 wires its own resume entry)"`. The pause-resume path is the blocking poll loop itself, not a separate later re-invocation.
- **Non-interactive caller support is opt-in and defaults to blocking**: `under_scheduler.auto_approve` (workflow-schema.md line ~448-456) — `true` auto-passes the pause step without dispatching the handler at all; `false` "fails closed with an error instead of blocking on a non-interactive pause." Doc states: "Interactive runs ignore `under_scheduler` and dispatch the pause step normally." This confirms the *default* assumption is an interactive session; headless/scheduler callers must explicitly opt out of the blocking wait via config, or get a hard failure — they cannot naturally "come back later" the way Minerva's `getRunStatus` polling model does.
- Graduation status (per `hive/decisions/001-executor-cutover.md`): pause-gate semantics reached production at Order 7 (`ui-design`, `design-review` workflows) and Order 9 (`daily-ceremony`, "plan-approval pause migration"). Executor is opt-in per-consumer/per-workflow (`executor: hive-dag` + `executor_default: true` in `.pHive/hive.config.yaml`, default OFF); no sunset date for the legacy orchestrator-narrated path.

**3. Runner-agnostic / headless work — broader landscape:**
- `mdostal/plugin-hive-fork` (the actual fork identity behind both the `fork` git remote and any "mdostal's fork" reference — GitHub confirms both `mdostal/plugin-hive` and `mdostal/plugin-hive-fork` resolve to the same repo, parent = firefly-events/plugin-hive) has **12 PRs**, several explicitly "runner-agnostic":
  - **PR #12** "feat(agnostic): runner-agnostic PLAN — port /plugin-hive:plan DECOMPOSE to opencode/gemini/codex" — **MERGED** 2026-08-09. Adds `hive/agnostic/{plan-decompose.prompt.md, adapters.mjs, plan-agnostic.mjs, README.md}`. This is **the exact CLI entrypoint Minerva's `agnostic-plan-driver.ts` spawns** (`hive/agnostic/plan-agnostic.mjs`). PR body explicitly names Minerva: *"minerva/src/agnostic-plan-driver.ts asks Heimdall /available-route?task-type=planning; on a non-claude route ... it spawns this entrypoint, else falls back to the built-in claude SpawnDriver."* PR body also states: *"Consider also targeting firefly-events/plugin-hive (upstream) — the port is generically useful, not fork-specific"* — i.e., as of merge, **not yet sent upstream**.
  - **PR #11** "feat: make /test+/review handoff runner-agnostic (last claude hardcode) + wire CI test gate" — MERGED.
  - **PR #6** "feat(backend): runner-agnostic OpenAI-compat backend (Kimi K3 + Gemini)" — MERGED.
  - **PR #3** "Runner-agnostic execution: codex headless backend + runtime-neutral process manifest (DOS-327/329/334)" — **MERGED**. This matches the local checkout's current branch content exactly: `hive/lib/codex-backend.mjs` (headless `codex exec --json --ephemeral` dispatcher, explicitly "non-cmux, non-interactive... does NOT depend on cmux, tmux, or any visible-pane infrastructure"), `hive/lib/process-manifest-loader.mjs`, `hive/manifests/{plan.process.yaml, process-manifest.schema.json}` — a declarative, "executor-neutral representation of the workflow" (`dispatch-parity.md`: *"any executor (CC plugin, Codex, direct API, hive-dag) can consume"* the manifest).
  - **PR #10** "Promote: dev -> main" — still **OPEN** (created 2026-08-02). This means the fork's `dev` branch (containing PRs #3, #6, #11, #12's work) has **not yet even been promoted to the fork's own `main`**, let alone sent as a PR to `firefly-events/plugin-hive` upstream. Confirmed via `gh api repos/mdostal/plugin-hive-fork/contents/hive/agnostic` on `main` → 404 (not present).
  - No PR in `firefly-events/plugin-hive` (checked via `--search "opencode"`, `--search "plan-agnostic"`, `--search "agnostic"`) matches this agnostic-planning-port work — **it exists only in the fork, not upstream**, distinct from PR #341 which specifically targets upstream.
- **"Heimdall" does not exist anywhere in plugin-hive** (canonical or fork; searched cache + checkout, zero hits). It is purely Minerva/Pantheon-side infrastructure — an external routing service Minerva's `agnostic-plan-driver.ts` calls (`GET {HEIMDALL_URL}/available-route?task-type=planning`, default `http://localhost:4870`). Fail-open by design: any network/parse/timeout error or non-claude-unavailable condition → `null` → Minerva keeps its built-in claude `SpawnDriver`.
- `dispatch-parity.md` documents plugin-hive's own existing multi-substrate concept (`default`/`multica`/`cc-workflows` columns, future `sandcastle`/`gh-actions-legacy`) predating this fork work — plugin-hive already had a notion of swappable execution substrates for its 6 orchestrator skills (plan/execute/test/design/design-review/review) before the DOS-327/329/334 process-manifest work generalized it.

## CONSTRAINTS

- PR #341's headless question protocol only covers kickoff/design/plan — not execute, test, review, ship, or any other Hive command surface Minerva might need to drive.
- The DAG executor's `node_type: pause` requires the executing process to physically block inside a `while` loop with `time.sleep()` for the pause duration (up to 30 days) — it is not a fresh-process-per-poll model. A caller wanting Minerva's "dispatch once, poll status later from a different process" shape must use `under_scheduler.auto_approve: false` to fail closed rather than block, and there's no built-in "reconnect and keep waiting" primitive for a caller that wasn't the one blocking.
- `node_type: pause` is scoped to the DAG executor runtime only, itself opt-in per-workflow/per-consumer (`executor_default: false` by default) and only graduated for `ui-design`, `design-review`, `daily-ceremony` per the cutover ADR — most Hive skills (kickoff, plan as invoked by Minerva today) do not run under this executor at all.
- The `hive/agnostic/plan-agnostic.mjs` CLI that Minerva's `agnostic-plan-driver.ts` depends on exists only on the fork's `dev` branch (not fork `main`, not upstream `firefly-events/plugin-hive` at all) — Minerva's candidate path list (`~/code/plugin-hive-fork`, `~/Code/plugin-hive-fork`, `~/.claude/plugins/plugin-hive/hive/agnostic/plan-agnostic.mjs`) currently resolves to **none of these on this machine** (verified: neither `~/code/plugin-hive-fork` nor `~/Code/plugin-hive-fork` exists; the plugin cache at `2.15.0` has no `hive/agnostic/` directory).

## RISKS

- **Minerva's "bulletproof claude fallback" is likely always triggering silently today.** `agnosticPlanCliPath()` returns `null` unless one of three hardcoded candidate paths exists; none do on this machine as checked. This means `resolveAgnosticPlanDriver()` is presently a no-op — the runner-agnostic PLAN driver code path may never have executed for real outside of the PR #12 author's own demo environment, undermining any claim that Minerva today benefits from cross-runtime planning.
- PR #341 has been open 18+ days (2026-07-26 → 2026-08-13, "today") with zero human review engagement — only automated CodeRabbit rounds and the author's own responses. Its "OPEN" status should not be read as "actively being reviewed"; it may be stalled awaiting a maintainer.
- The native pause mechanism's blocking-poll-loop design means it cannot straightforwardly serve as "the thing that replaces Minerva's ABI" for an agentic harness that wants to dispatch-and-walk-away (e.g., a scheduler, a CI job, another LLM harness checking back periodically without holding a process open) — this is a structural, not incidental, gap relative to the north_star's bar ("any harness that can pause and resume").
- Fork-vs-upstream state is easy to conflate: work described as "plugin-hive is gaining native agnostic pause/resume" (per north_star) is scattered across (a) an open, unreviewed upstream PR (#341, headless *questions*, not pause/resume of the DAG-executor kind), (b) a merged-but-unpromoted fork branch (`dev`, not yet on fork `main`) implementing headless *runtime dispatch* (codex/opencode backends) with no pause/resume relationship, and (c) an already-shipped (2.15.0, installed) DAG-executor pause primitive that is unrelated to either of the above and is synchronous/blocking, not headless-orchestrator-friendly by default.

## UTILITIES_AVAILABLE

- `hive/lib/dag_executor/pause/` (token generation/verification, signal polling) — reusable Python primitives if a future integration wanted to speak the same sentinel-file protocol from outside the DAG executor.
- `hive/lib/question_gateway.{py,js}` (PR #341, unmerged) — envelope format explicitly designed to be orchestrator-answerable in a shape the PR author states already matches Minerva's `submitAnswers`.
- `hive/manifests/process-manifest.schema.json` + `plan.process.yaml` (fork, unmerged upstream) — a declarative workflow-as-data format an external harness could in principle parse without any Claude Code plugin runtime at all, if this pattern is extended.

## EXTERNAL_REFERENCES

- https://github.com/firefly-events/plugin-hive/pull/341 (Headless question protocol + bounded Stop hook, OPEN)
- https://github.com/firefly-events/plugin-hive/pull/39 (dag-executor foundation incl. resume/pause, MERGED — hde-0..2, 5-8)
- https://github.com/mdostal/plugin-hive-fork/pull/12 (runner-agnostic PLAN port, MERGED 2026-08-09)
- https://github.com/mdostal/plugin-hive-fork/pull/3 (codex headless backend + process manifest, DOS-327/329/334, MERGED)
- https://github.com/mdostal/plugin-hive-fork/pull/11 (test+review handoff runner-agnostic, MERGED)
- https://github.com/mdostal/plugin-hive-fork/pull/6 (runner-agnostic OpenAI-compat backend, MERGED)
- https://github.com/mdostal/plugin-hive-fork/pull/10 (Promote: dev -> main, OPEN since 2026-08-02 — gates all of the above from reaching even the fork's own main)

## UNANSWERED_QUESTIONS

- Does `hive/agnostic/plan-agnostic.mjs` (PR #12) actually function as a substitute for Minerva's own kickoff/plan question-and-answer loop, or only for the single-shot DECOMPOSE write? (Only checked the PR description/proof snippet, not the full adapters.mjs/plan-agnostic.mjs source.)
- Whether `node_type: pause`'s sentinel-file protocol could be driven by a non-Claude-Code, non-interactive harness in practice was not fully resolved by code alone — the `under_scheduler.auto_approve` doc strongly implies "no" by default (fails closed rather than adapting), but no test or example of a real non-interactive caller successfully using it was found in the time available.
- Not verified whether PR #341's `hive/references/kickoff-protocol.md` / `question-envelope-schema.md` prose actually documents interop guidance for an external ABI like Minerva's, versus only describing plugin-hive-internal behavior.
- Did not check `firefly-events/plugin-hive` issue tracker or Slack/external discussion for maintainer sentiment on PR #341 (only GitHub PR comments were available via `gh`).

## INCONSISTENCY_RISK_SIGNALS

- North_star's framing ("plugin-hive is gaining native agnostic pause/resume") conflates three distinct, non-overlapping pieces of work (headless *questions* PR #341; headless *runtime dispatch* fork PRs #3/#6/#11/#12; native DAG-executor `pause` node type) that differ in maturity (unreviewed-open / merged-but-unpromoted / shipped-but-blocking-and-narrow-scope respectively) and in mechanism (none of the three is a stateless dispatch-then-poll-later ABI the way Minerva's `startRun`/`getRunStatus` is).
- Minerva's `agnostic-plan-driver.ts` code comments assert Heimdall routing and the ported CLI as working infrastructure ("BULLETPROOF CLAUDE FALLBACK"), but the dependency (`hive/agnostic/plan-agnostic.mjs`) is unreachable via any of its three hardcoded candidate paths on this machine — the described behavior and the actual resolvable state appear to have diverged.

## VALIDATION NOTE

Source: codebase-only (internal repo research across two local checkouts, one plugin cache directory, and `gh` CLI queries against GitHub's API for firefly-events/plugin-hive and mdostal/plugin-hive-fork). No external library/package documentation was consulted; not applicable here.
